body:
I had thought my skills in eyeballing mushrooms were adequate for some reason. However, that wasn't the case. I chewed up the substance with determination, eager to explore the depths of my chosen selection. Opting to consume them dry, without even water to aid in swallowing, as if that would enhance my trip or connect me to some ancient indigenous ritual I was ignorant of at the time.
Having immersed myself in Terence McKenna's teachings, I came across the concept of the heroic dose  "5 grams and the darkness," as mentioned in (name the speech). I saw it as a challenge, as if I had something to prove to fellow psychonauts I wasn't communicating with at the time. Donning my sleep mask, I lay down, feeling as though I was thrust into an archetypal jungle, repeatedly consumed by its depths.
A savage inner voice echoed, insisting I shouldn't be there, that I had made a massive mistake. It pointed out the irony of my past racism, labeling it the most pathetic thing it had ever witnessed. My psyche was torn apart by absolute hatred, contempt, and bitterness. In the usual darkness of my closed eyes, I saw a black panther staring at me with yellow eyes and fangs  simultaneously menacing yet a tame observer.
Lines of connectivity stretched before me, a 3D network where I realized I was one of these lines, parallel but unconnected. Gradually, intense pain enveloped my brain as giant needles pierced through, pulsating sharply. I thought I was experiencing some form of death, unaware of psychosomatic physical pains. Despite the agony, I accepted the experience, gripping the covers to resist banging my head into the wall to end it.
Convinced it was a drug-induced state that would eventually conclude, I opened my eyes to witness the room taking on an ugly, negative tint. A yellow triangle, square, and circle appeared, conveying something I couldn't grasp. Reluctantly, I closed my eyes again, continuing the internal journey for what felt like an hour and thirty minutes. The passing of time remained unclear, but I sensed it was still daylight, albeit darker.
The experience concluded with my mind soothing me in the best possible way. It informed me that everything it had deconstructed in a controlled manner was, in fact, mendable. I had erred by going against my true principles, shaped by conditioning from my community and especially my family. The past was deemed irrelevant, and this self-healing of my mind altered the trajectory of where I would have otherwise ended up.
